findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: the packet omits read_bounded_regular_file, the limit definitions, aggregate accounting/rejection, and the complete rejection tests. These are necessary to establish that the enlarged read remains bounded and oversized packages still fail. In particular, a package check after reading can permit more bytes to be read before rejection when the per-file cap increases, so the plan's unchanged-total-read-bound claim is not established.
findings.smallest_fix: Supply frozen context for the helper, constants, complete hashing loop, and rejection assertions. Distinguish the accepted-package size ceiling from the maximum bytes read before rejection in the plan.

findings.failure_path: Both ledger hashes use zero-filled files with different lengths. A faulty implementation hashing only the first MiB plus file size would pass this assertion while ignoring same-length edits in the newly accepted suffix. Thus the test does not prove its stated content-binding property.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a same-length mutation of a byte beyond the first MiB and assert that the digest changes, retaining the size-boundary cases.

challenge_focus: The review controller refused every candidate that adds a source-register row, because the append-only ledger reached the 1,048,576-byte bound applied to each file of a selected skill package. The change bounds a selected-skill file by the package ceiling instead. Check that the read stays bounded, that no other input lost its bound, that the changed and added test cases would fail without the change and still reject an oversized file and an oversized package, and that the plan states only what was verified.
